Soitec soars more than 15% in Paris: driven by AI and its wafers for light, its operating profit triples, a year after the crash

On Thursday 19 November, shares in Soitec, the silicon wafer maker based in the Isère region, jumped more than 15% in Paris, the best performance on the European STOXX 600 index. The evening before, the group reported €317 million in half-year sales (+39%) and targeted around 40% growth for the fiscal year, above expectations [1][2][3].

In the first half of its fiscal year 2027 (April-September 2026), Soitec posted €317 million in revenue, compared with €231 million a year earlier: +39% at constant scope and exchange rates, +37% as reported [3]. The second quarter alone reached €204 million, up 50% [3].

The engine is silicon photonics (Photonics-SOI): wafers used to make components that carry data by light inside artificial intelligence data centres. Its sales reached about $125 million over the half-year, compared with about $50 million a year earlier [2].
Current operating income rose from €11 million (4.7% of sales) to €35 million (11.0%) [3]. According to Investing.com, earnings per share came in at €0.80 [4].

For the full fiscal year, which ends on 31 March 2027, Soitec is targeting growth of around 40%, well above what analysts expected, according to Reuters as carried by Boursorama [1]. The group had not given an annual forecast since May 2025; it is doing so again because it can see its orders through to the end of the year, BFM Bourse reports [5].

Chief executive Laurent Remont, who joined from Infineon in April to replace Pierre Barnabé [6], highlighted customers already committed through capacity reservation agreements running until 2028 [1].

At around 10:36 Paris time, the stock was up about 15% [1]; it had gained 15.34% shortly after the open, leading the SBF 120 [7]. The bank UBS, which upgraded its rating, now targets €130 per share instead of €94, and expects photonics to account for half of group sales by fiscal year 2029 [8].

The key point: on the stock market, a company is worth what it promises for tomorrow more than what it earned yesterday. Soitec is jumping less for its half-year than for its +40% forecast for the year, which beats market estimates [1][5].

It is also the story of a turnaround. Almost exactly a year ago, Soitec collapsed 30% in one session, to its lowest since 2016, after a 36% drop in quarterly sales [9][10]. Its historic speciality, wafers for smartphones and cars, was suffering. Photonics for AI is taking over.

For France, it is a rare signal: an industrial company born near Grenoble is benefiting directly from the global AI race, like the American chip giants. But UBS warns that its own forecasts assume almost flawless execution and a Soitec market share above 85% over the long term [8].

If your savings include funds of French mid-caps or European technology, Soitec carries weight in them. Above all, remember the lesson: a stock that has fallen a lot can rebound very quickly when the company restores visibility, but that rebound rests on promises that still have to come true.

How it works: why a forecast moves a share price more than a result

A share price reflects what investors think the company will earn in the years ahead. A good half-year is already in the past: what changes the price is the gap between what the company announces for the future and what the market expected. Soitec announces around 40% growth for the year when analysts forecast less [1]: they all recalculate their estimates, and the stock rises to the new price judged fair. After a long period without an annual forecast, since May 2025 [5], simply giving a course again is also reassuring: uncertainty falls, and investors are willing to pay more. The reverse is true: in November 2025, disappointing forecasts had wiped 30% off the stock in one day [10].
Precedents: Soitec, a roller coaster driven by its forecasts
20 November 2025

After a 36% fall in its second-quarter sales, including −68% in automotive, and an outlook judged disappointing by Oddo BHF, Soitec lost 30.09% at the close, to €24.12, its lowest since December 2016 [9][10].
The stock had already lost nearly 70% since the start of 2025: when a chip company disappoints about the future, the penalty is brutal [10].
May 2025
Soitec stops publishing annual forecasts and only gives quarter-by-quarter targets [5][10].
Without an annual course, investors were flying blind; its return on Thursday is one of the reasons for the stock's jump [5].
To understand, not advice to buy or sell.
Soitec
Half-year sales up 39% and a forecast of around 40% annual growth, above expectations; the stock was up about 15% on Thursday morning in Paris, according to Reuters [1][3].

Walmart raises its targets for the third time this year, but stays more cautious than Wall Street ahead of the holidays

On Thursday 19 November, Walmart, the world's largest retailer, reported $188.8 billion in quarterly sales and adjusted earnings of 65 cents per share, slightly above expectations. It raised its annual forecasts for the third time this year, but by less than analysts had hoped: the stock was only up about 1% before the open [1][2].

In the third quarter of its fiscal year 2027 (August-October 2026), revenue reached $188.8 billion, against $187.38 billion expected according to FactSet, cited by AP [1]. It grew 5.2% year on year [3].
Adjusted earnings per share came in at 65 cents, against 64 cents expected by Wall Street [1].
Comparable sales (in store and online, excluding openings) rose 2.9%, better than the 2.6% of the previous quarter [1]. The group's online sales jumped 17% [3].
For the full fiscal year, Walmart now targets sales growth of 4.9% to 5.2%, against 4% to 5% until now [1], and adjusted earnings per share of $2.84 to $2.89, against $2.80 to $2.87 [2].

It is the third forecast increase of the year, but these targets are more cautious than industry analysts expected, according to AP [1]. The stock was up nearly 1% before the Wall Street open according to AP, 0.6% according to Investing.com [1][2].

Before these results, Walmart's stock had gained about 13% since the start of the year, according to CNBC [4]. The day before, its rival Target gained 6.1% in the session after beating expectations, according to MarketBeat [8].

The key point: Walmart, the world's largest retailer, serves as a thermometer of American consumption. Sales up 5.2% and accelerating comparable sales (2.9% after 2.6%) at the start of the holiday season say that Americans keep spending [1][3].

But the market expected more than "slightly better" forecasts. When a company beats expectations by only one cent, as here (65 against 64), and cautiously raises its course, the stock moves little: the good result was already priced in [1][2].

This caution is a habit at Walmart. In February 2026, for the first results of its new boss John Furner, the group had already given a lower-than-expected course and its stock had fallen, before raising its targets three times since [5][1]. Some analysts see it as a strategy: setting a bar that is easy to clear [5].

Walmart is one of the biggest companies in the American indices found in many savings funds. Its figures show that American consumption is holding up, but its caution shows it is wary of the months ahead.

How it works: "beating expectations" and the game of cautious forecasts

Before each release, analysts estimate what the company will earn: the average of their figures is called the consensus (here 64 cents per share according to AP) [1]. The stock reacts to the gap between the published figure and that consensus, and above all to the targets the company gives for the future. A company that sets cautious targets has a better chance of beating them later, quarter after quarter; that is what the bank D.A. Davidson suspected at Walmart in February: "setting a beatable bar" [5]. The drawback: on the day the course is given, it can disappoint, and the price dips a little, as in February 2026 [5].
Precedents: Walmart, solid results and displayed caution
19 February 2026

For the first results of John Furner, who became chief executive on 1 February, Walmart reported $190.7 billion in fourth-quarter sales (+5.6%), but forecast only 3.5% to 4.5% sales growth for the year [5].
The stock fell more than 3% before the open, then closed down 1.38% at $124.87: investors looked at the course more than at the quarter [5].
20 November 2025
Walmart reported $179.5 billion in quarterly sales (+5.8%) and adjusted earnings of 62 cents per share against 60 expected, with American online sales up 28% [6].
That time, the stock jumped before the open: a result clearly beating expectations, with raised targets, is rewarded [6].
To understand, not advice to buy or sell.

news.2026-11-19-canada-carney-trump-shen: Canada: in Shenzhen, Carney gets 20 minutes with Trump and a promise to resume work on a trade deal

On the evening of Wednesday 18 November, on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney met Donald Trump for about twenty minutes. The two leaders agreed to keep working towards a trade deal, with no timetable, three months after negotiations broke down [1][2][3].
According to Carney's office, the two teams discussed a "mutually beneficial" agreement that creates jobs and respects Canada's languages, culture and sovereignty [1][3].
"We have been making progress," Carney told reporters; Trump gave no date for a formal resumption of negotiations [1].
Carney says Canada's trade with China is not at the top of Trump's "hierarchy of issues", while the White House criticises this rapprochement [1][2].
Since talks failed in August, Washington has applied 50% tariffs on almost $30 billion of Canadian goods; autos and steel remain the sticking points [1].

The key point: Canada is playing on two fronts. A few days after meeting Xi Jinping and securing cuts in Chinese duties on Canadian pork and seafood, Carney is re-engaging with Washington, its biggest customer [1].

The stakes are high: since August, the 50% duties have hit almost $30 billion of Canadian goods, and autos and steel, at the heart of the economies of Ontario and Quebec, are waiting for an outcome [1].

For you, it is an example of how middle-sized countries try to negotiate between China and the United States. The fate of the Canadian car industry, closely tied to American factories, is being decided in these talks.

news.2026-11-19-argentine-milei-devaluat: Argentina: Milei rules out any devaluation of the peso and admits the country could soon announce a "technical recession"

Argentine President Javier Milei called the rumours of a peso devaluation "nonsense" on Wednesday 18 November on the A24 channel. The day before, in front of the central bank, he had acknowledged that a "technical recession", two quarters of economic contraction, could be announced soon [1][2][3].
Questioned by journalist Eduardo Feinmann, Milei called the rumours of a jump in the dollar a "tontería" (nonsense), and said that those who call for a devaluation end up calling for low wages [3].
He explained that inflation is not falling faster because of the war in the Middle East and what he calls the "kuka risk", the markets' fear of a return of the Peronist opposition [1].

On 17 November, at the central bank's Monetary and Banking Conference, he admitted that a "technical recession" could be announced "shortly" [2]; his Economy Minister, Luis Caputo, acknowledged that growth is weaker than expected [4].
He also acknowledged that, with 32% poverty, some Argentines "struggle to make ends meet", before speaking instead of "privations" [3].
The key point: Milei refuses to devalue so as not to reignite inflation, even if it means the economy slows down [1][3].
The bet is political: Milei, running for re-election in 2027, says he will win in the first round [2], while his government admits that growth is weaker than expected [4].
For you, Argentina is a textbook case: a peso kept strong brings inflation down but weighs on activity and jobs, a trade-off familiar to every country that defends its currency.
